clue.text: Cook can keep joint under this cover

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct or fiddle it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter by letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: the roast joint stays warm in the pot with the lid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' and 'joint' paint a kitchen scene with a roast, but 'Cook' rearranges CAN KEEP, and the joint is the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the small bone that shields the front of the knee, so the knee joint lies beneath it.

clue.text: Family doctor at home — the most important person

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
in means at home, not out

explanation.surface: The family doctor, when home, is the boss of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one phrase but splits in two; GP (general practitioner) is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A central figure without whom an organisation collapses, like the bolt in a mechanism, is the key person.

clue.text: Destroy and rip out contents of former gallery

indicators.note: the rearranged letters become the contents of the former gallery, placed inside it

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: rip out suggests tearing apart, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vandal wrecks and guts what used to be an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the torn word to IRP, and 'contents of' sets it inside the former gallery after its first T. The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out and wipe out completely is to destroy, a synonym.

clue.text: This creature makes us shy, rising in the saddle

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: up means on horseback, as a jockey is up

explanation.surface: An animal makes riders nervous as it rears up under the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the riding word upwards, as befits a down clue. A jockey who is riding is said to be 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large South American rodent, also called nutria, so it is an animal.

clue.text: One retired to a boarding house with hesitation

parts.note: a pension is a continental boarding house or small hotel
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped working hesitantly moves into a lodging house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired to' reads as moving into, but 'One retired' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receiving an allowance after leaving work is a retired person, a description.

clue.text: An early colonist's decisive argument

explanation.surface: A pioneer's clinching point in a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer who sets up home in new land is one sense; a remark that ends a dispute once and for all is the other.

clue.text: Waves on saying goodbye to one active in the theatre?

indicators.note: on says goodbye to the larger word, leaving it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a surgeon works in an operating theatre, hence the question mark
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor waves as he bids farewell to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell or rush of water is a wave, so the plural noun matches a verb or noun sense of rolling waves.

clue.text: Cheat has disturbed rest after cards

indicators.note: the rearranged rest comes after the cards in the answer

parts.note: a trick is the set of cards played in one round

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up and put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cardsharp cheats, and his rest after the card game is troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' makes STER of the four letters; 'after' puts them behind the cards. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A con man who deceives people is a swindler or cheat.

clue.text: See a donkey caught with this

definitions.text: See a donkey caught with this

indicators.note: the animal is caught inside the exclamation, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Look how a donkey is roped by a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a rope loop used to catch an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose is thrown to capture livestock, so an animal is caught with it.

clue.text: Decide to have another go at the crossword?

definitions.text: have another go at the crossword?

explanation.surface: Making up your mind to try the puzzle again.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up one's mind is one sense; to work out the puzzle a second time, read as re-solve, is the other.

clue.text: Spruce seen in plantation at Tynemouth

indicators.note: the letters can be seen inside the run of words plantation at Tynemouth

explanation.surface: A spruce tree growing in a plantation on the north-east coast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree to match the plantation, but it is the adjective meaning smart. Tynemouth is a town at the mouth of the River Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and smartly dressed, a synonym.

clue.text: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image

definitions.text: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image

parts.words: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image
parts.note: the youth of Greek myth who fell for his own reflection made a blunder and was turned into a flower: bloomer means both a mistake and a plant in flower

explanation.surface: Someone made a howler through vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the vain youth who loved his reflection was changed into the flower that bears his name, a cryptic description of both.

clue.text: Seen around Uttar Pradesh — piglike creature with spines

indicators.note: the piglike word is seen wrapped round the state's abbreviation, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: porcine means like a pig
UP is the standard abbreviation for the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh

explanation.surface: A traveller in northern India spots a strange piggy animal covered in spines.
explanation.definitionFit: This large rodent is protected by a coat of sharp quills, so it is a spined animal.

clue.text: Funeral bell once heard from a small hill

explanation.surface: A tolling bell drifts down from a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic spelling for the sound of a passing bell is now used only for a rounded mound; 'once' flags the old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for the tolling of a death bell is one sense; a hillock or mound is the other.

clue.text: Husband chasing cow in South Wales?

indicators.note: one piece chases another by coming behind it, so the husband's letter goes after the cow

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, a cow or ox
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy tables

explanation.surface: A farmer runs after a stray cow somewhere in the Welsh valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, hence the question mark: the answer is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a town near Swansea in the south of the principality, a geographical example.

clue.text: Advantage for a racehorse or the principal's floozie

parts.note: a head is a school principal; the possessive gives the s
tart is slang for a floozie or loose woman

explanation.surface: A school scandal: the horse's lead versus the principal's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead given at the beginning of a race is an advantage, a metaphor from racing.

clue.text: Bargain to get across

explanation.surface: Haggling to make a crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To haggle or work out a deal is one sense; to pass over or through an obstacle successfully is the other.

clue.text: Boasting more suitable for a skilled man

parts.note: gas is empty talk or boasting
fitter means more fit, more suitable

explanation.surface: Showing off makes someone better qualified for a craftsman's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who installs and repairs fuel appliances is a skilled worker.

clue.text: Roam endlessly, wearing an old emperor's fur

indicators.note: the trimmed roaming word is worn within the emperor phrase, so it goes inside

parts.note: an gives the single letter of the indefinite article
a khan was a Mongol or Tatar emperor

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to stray is to roam

explanation.surface: Wandering about clad in a past ruler's fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the roaming word, leaving STRA; 'wearing' puts that inside the emperor phrase, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is curly lambskin from Central Asia, prized as a fur.

clue.text: A ruse, thus rewriting a dictionary

indicators.note: rewriting the words gives their letters in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scheme to rewrite a dictionary under false pretences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' rearranges the letters of A RUSE and THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is a kind of word-reference, loosely called a dictionary of words grouped by meaning.

clue.text: "So musical a discord, such sweet ——" (M.N. Dream)

definitions.text: "So musical a discord, such sweet ——" (M.N. Dream)

parts.words: "So musical a discord, such sweet ——" (M.N. Dream)
parts.note: the missing word completes Hippolyta's line about hounds baying in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 4

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's comedy about the cry of hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the hounds' cry is compared to a rumbling noise from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippolyta compares the hounds' baying to the deep rumble of a storm, a literary quotation.

clue.text: Relation depriving Nelson of his house

indicators.note: depriving Nelson of something takes those letters out of his name

parts.note: Horatio was the first name of Admiral Nelson

explanation.surface: A family member who robbed the admiral of his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' suggests a relative, but it means a proportion between quantities. Nelson is Britain's most famous admiral, Horatio Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between two quantities is a numerical relationship, a synonym.

clue.text: Supervise lines replacing the centre of one

indicators.note: the middle letter of one is swapped out for the lines

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A manager has one worker's middle shift covered by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: VERSE takes the place of N, the middle letter of ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch over and direct work is to supervise, a synonym.

clue.text: Presses 5 dn to move head to tail

indicators.note: the first letter of the referred answer is shifted from the front to the end

parts.note: the answer to 5 Down is the word for waves rushing forward

explanation.surface: Urging a referred word to rearrange itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 5 Down has its first letter carried to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to push or exhort them, a synonym.

clue.text: Fishing-spear employed at first in indiscreet act

parts.note: a gaff is a hooked spear for landing large fish

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word employed

explanation.surface: Using a fishing spear first was a tactless move.
explanation.definitionFit: A social blunder or tactless remark is an indiscretion.

clue.text: Container made of new fibre, as found in church

indicators.note: a new version of fibre is its letters made over in another order
as is found inside the church abbreviation, so it sits between those letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bag woven from fresh fibre turns up in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes BRIEF of the fibre; 'found in' puts the two-letter word inside the Church of England abbreviation. 'made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat case for carrying papers is a kind of container.

clue.text: Pipe-lines? That's right

parts.note: BR is British Rail, whose railway lines are abbreviated so
that is, Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that pipelines are indeed what is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe-lines' looks like one word, but Pipe is the definition and lines is BR, British Rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco pipes are carved from the root of the heath plant of that name, so a pipe made from it shares the name.

clue.text: Swiftly-moving vessels

explanation.surface: A description of fast ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast or nimble is one sense; a group of ships sailing together, a navy, is the other.

clue.text: Valorous deed dividing believer and one expecting failure

indicators.note: the brave act splits the believer in two by sitting inside the word

parts.note: a deist believes in God on the basis of reason
a feat is a brave or remarkable deed

explanation.surface: A heroic act drives a wedge between a man of faith and a pessimist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' splits the believer after DE, with the brave act in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who anticipates losing and gives up in advance is a pessimist, so the description is a paraphrase.

clue.text: Moral significance, albeit in French art

indicators.note: albeit sits inside French art, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: es is French for art in the old sense of are, as in tu es, thou art
albeit means although, shortened to tho

explanation.surface: Moral meaning, even if expressed in French painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is not painting but the verb: French tu es is 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or moral character of a group or work is a near-synonym of moral significance.

clue.text: Come in again to make another record

explanation.surface: Coming back in to log a second entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back into a room is one sense; to write an item into a ledger or register a second time is the other.

clue.text: Train crash in Orient? True

indicators.note: a crash throws the letters into a new jumble

parts.note: taken as written
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rail disaster in the East: is the report accurate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' and 'crash' suggest a railway accident; 'crash' rearranges IN, E (East, from Orient) and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can mean a body of attendants following an important person, as with an entourage.
